title: IndentationError
kicker: Python for SDFs · Fix the error
traceback: IndentationError: expected an indented block after 'for' statement on line 2

notes.label: IndentationError
notes.text: The type of error. The spaces at the start of a line aren't what Python expects. Like a SyntaxError, it stops the whole cell before anything runs.

notes.label: expected an indented block after 'for' statement on line 2
notes.text: The reason. The line after a `for ...:` line has to be pushed in, usually by 4 spaces. That's how Python knows which lines repeat.

notes.label: on line 2
notes.text: The message says line 2 because that's the for line that needs a body. The line to fix is line 3.

notes.label: line 3, and the ^
notes.text: There's no ----> arrow here either. The top line names line 3, and the ^ sits under the start of `print(lot)`, the line that should be indented.

fixes.label: print(lot)
fixes.title: Best fix
fixes.feedback: Four spaces tell Python that `print(lot)` belongs to the loop, so it prints all three lot numbers. Colab indents for you when you press Enter after a colon. Pasted code is where indents usually go wrong.

fixes.label: for lot in lot_numbers:
fixes.title: Wrong line
fixes.feedback: Now line 2 is indented when nothing asked for it, so you get IndentationError: unexpected indent. Line 3 is the one that needs to move in.

fixes.label: for lot in lot_numbers
fixes.title: Now it's a SyntaxError
fixes.feedback: The colon was right. Without it Python reports expected ':', and line 3 still isn't indented.
fixes.fixed_code:
lot_numbers = ["A2307-114", "B2311-052", "C2402-007"]
for lot in lot_numbers
print(lot)

_note: traceback from IPython 7.34 / Python 3.12 (kernel output, only the temp-file path shortened to <ipython-input-2>); confirm against a live Colab run. SyntaxError and IndentationError are reported before the cell runs, so IPython prints a File/line header and a ^ caret instead of a ----> arrow
